_comment: delta-rs is pinned by COMMIT, not by published version. At acquisition time (2026-09-15),
the published deltalake line targeted arrow 58 / datafusion 53; this retained commit uses arrow 59 /
datafusion 55 / object_store 0.13.2. docs.rs therefore has nothing to serve for this pin,
so build/acquire.py produces the rustdoc JSON locally and build.py reads it offline.
--all-features is impossible here: rustls and native-tls are mutually exclusive and both
forward to delta_kernel_default_engine. Every features_on list below is the set cargo
ACTUALLY resolved (read from `cargo doc -Z unstable-options --unit-graph`), not the set
this file asked for -- resolver 3 unifies upward, so the two differ.

repository.name: deltalake
repository.title: delta-rs and the Delta kernel
repository.description: Pinned API surface, guides and examples for delta-rs main @58f07cd6, on arrow 59 / datafusion 55 / object_store 0.13.2.

git.lock_note: delta-rs does not commit Cargo.lock and takes the kernel from branch buoyant/main. The branch is not a pin; lock_deps is the assertion that acquisition resolved the kernel this file names.

features_off.native-tls: mutually exclusive with rustls; upstream's own docs.rs metadata says the same
features_off.python: enables arrow/pyarrow only; zero cfg(feature) sites in any delta-rs src
features_off.opendal-s3: gates only a register_handlers arm, no item surface
features_off.opendal-gcs: gates only a register_handlers arm, no item surface
features_off.opendal-azblob: gates only a register_handlers arm, no item surface
features_off.opendal-azdls: gates only a register_handlers arm, no item surface
features_off.opendal-oss: gates only a register_handlers arm, no item surface
features_off.opendal-obs: gates only a register_handlers arm, no item surface
features_off.opendal-cos: gates only a register_handlers arm, no item surface
features_off.opendal-tos: gates only a register_handlers arm, no item surface
features_off.opendal-b2: gates only a register_handlers arm, no item surface
features_off.opendal-swift: gates only a register_handlers arm, no item surface
features_off.opendal-webhdfs: gates only a register_handlers arm, no item surface
features_off.opendal-webdav: gates only a register_handlers arm, no item surface
features_off.opendal-hf: gates only a register_handlers arm, no item surface
features_off.opendal-ftp: native FTP dependency; gates only a register_handlers arm
features_off.opendal-sftp: native libssh2 dependency; gates only a register_handlers arm
features_off.opendal-fs: on at the deltalake-opendal level, where it is a default
features_off.opendal-memory: on at the deltalake-opendal level, where it is a default

features_off.delta-cache: zero cfg(feature) sites in crates/core/src; pulls foyer and tempfile for no item surface
features_off.datafusion-ext: an alias for `datafusion`, which is on; enabling it changes no cfg
features_off.humantime: optional dependency of cloud, which is on; the feature itself is not a cfg gate

crates.note: 127 cfg(feature = "datafusion") sites -- this is the feature that decides whether the DataFusion seam exists at all. 54 nanosecond-timestamps sites, of which 4 are not(feature = ...), so enabling it removes a small amount of surface as well as adding a large amount.
zero cfg(feature) sites in src: the documented surface is complete regardless of the tls choice
zero cfg(feature) sites in src; backed by pure-Rust hdfs-native-object-store, so no JVM or libhdfs is involved
documented as a crate although the deltalake facade has no `mount` feature and does not re-export it: reachable only by depending on deltalake-mount directly

features_off.opendal-s3: every opendal-* service feature gates only a register_handlers arm; none adds an item
features_off.opendal-ftp: service registration only; native FTP dependency
features_off.opendal-sftp: service registration only; native libssh2 dependency

crates.note: the only backend crate with real cfg gating: aws/azure/gcp/r2 have 5 sites each and datafusion 3, and several are not(feature = ...) variants, so enabling all four removes those alternatives

features_off.declarative-plans: experimental; not enabled by delta-rs and needs prost-build
features_off.test-utils: not enabled by delta-rs; would expose test-only constructors as public
features_off.column-defaults-in-dev: in-progress work; not enabled by delta-rs

crates.note: Documented under delta-rs's OWN unified feature selection, by naming it with -p inside the delta-rs workspace, not as a separate build. That is deliberate: an all-features kernel would advertise items a deltalake user cannot reach. internal-api (47 cfg sites) flips crc, column_trie, utils, path and log_replay from pub(crate) to pub, and delta-rs relies on that.

excluded_members.deltalake-test: test harness, not a capability surface
excluded_members.deltalake-python: cdylib with doc = false, and its [lib] name is `deltalake` -- the same as the facade, so documenting the workspace wholesale would have one silently overwrite the other
excluded_members.deltalake-derive: proc-macro crate whose sole export is the DeltaConfig derive. rustdoc format 61 emits no `paths` entry for #[proc_macro_derive] exports, so a derive macro cannot be indexed by canonical path at all; measured, documenting it yields one module and zero items. It is used only inside deltalake-core and is not re-exported to callers.
excluded_members.buoyant_kernel_derive: proc-macro crate in the kernel's own workspace. Measured, it holds two indexable items (`#[internal_api]` and `parse_column_name!`), both internal to the kernel's build; its three derives are invisible for the same rustdoc reason as above.

corpora.name: tests
corpora.note: Labelled tests, not examples. delta-rs ships 8 example files; the integration suite is where the real usage evidence is.

corpora.name: protocol
corpora.note: The normative Delta protocol specification: the authority for table features and log actions, which delta-rs implements rather than defines.
